official_gallery.comment: The university associates the photographs with its Schereschewsky Hall article. Entries 8 and 11 have no individual caption, alt, title or direction. The gallery duplicates items 0 and 1 at 3 and 9, respectively.

school-11.observed: Across the water after dark. Two return faces meet at a hipped-roof corner. Ground and upper windows share rounded heads; the bays are partly covered by trees and darkness.
school-11.attribution: The official gallery identifies the building at article level only. The exact wall, facing direction and two end bay limits are not independently labelled by the five additional public pages retrieved. A separate published Mann Hall night view (official photograph 11 for that building) has three visible storeys and is a different image.

school-08.observed: Cherry blossom hides much of a projecting two-storey facade with round-headed windows, narrow paired upper sashes and a small upturned roof. The photographed masonry is distinct from the shallow segmental-headed south courtyard sashes beside the tower.
school-08.attribution: The small roof could mark an external projecting bay, but neither end of the wing nor the clock appears in this crop. No authenticated direction for this pane.

two_small_courts.evidence: The single courtyard adjacent to the clock and main entrance matches the large grass/plinth courtyard. Beyond its opposite three-bay cross-wing is the northern yard, divided by a north–south connecting wing into one eastern and one western smaller void. District aerial shows both. Position is legible from the shared clock, roof ridge and the neighboring water tower.
two_small_courts.geometry_scope: No measured rear-elevation apertures follow from a roof outline.
